title: Bringing Cassandra Back
summary: Cassandra de Rolo fell to a dragon at Kraghammer and lingered in limbo while the party carried her across Vasselheim. At the Temple of Sarenrae, Pike Trickfoot drove Mortis's diamond into her chest and she breathed again — pale, exhausted and racked by migraines, remembering nothing of her death. Percy flew in to her bedside and offered the party passage; they still mean to see her home to Whitestone, his last stop, after a short detour to Sarenrae's ancient temple.

title: Pelor's Charge
summary: Pelor set Sorfon to carry the sealed censer of incense some seven kilometres across Vasselheim, from the Temple of Pelor to the Temple of Sarenrae, and to guard the surviving de Rolos. The custodian Marco granted the party pilgrim rites and kept Cassandra's body overnight. The urn has now reached the Temple of Sarenrae: Sorfon handed it to Pike Trickfoot, and since she does not belong to that temple it is meant for the temple itself. Guarding the de Rolos — Cassandra alive again, Percy at her side — remains his charge.

title: The Raven Queen's Thread
summary: A golden thread from Mortis's patron keeps singling out what he needs — it led him to Greyskull Keep and, in Vasselheim, to the scroll of Speak with Dead. Prayed to at the palace shrine of all gods, she answered through her shadar-kai and gave up Pike's hiding place. Mortis has since died by his own hand to stand before her in the Shadowfell and been raised again: they were lovers when she was mortal and he was Morgas, and she names negating him her one error. She wants the main mission finished first — Cassandra revived, then Whitestone.

title: Hunted and Watched
summary: An invisible imp spying at Ubu's feet named its master: La Toma, the Slayer's Take, a monster-hunter guild quartered in the war district — and they are hunting Mortis. Since Sorfon bought their dampir prisoner off them, they hunt Locus too; the contract lifts only once their leader Ocisa (?) is dealt with. Sarenrae herself has now asked that Locus be got out of the city and away from them. Mortis now believes that imp lied about La Toma to shield its true master; Fungrim (?), for his part, says he is trying to join La Toma for the money.

title: The Redeemed Dampir
summary: La Toma seized a white-haired dampir named Locus out of the crowd on the main avenue; Sorfon paid the orc Hungar (?) the 200 gp bounty to claim him, meaning to redeem rather than kill him. Baba Yaga's book names him the last living subject of a Strahd and Baba Yaga line bred as vampire monster-hunters, and he is bound by a Geas. Sarenrae, reached by holy-water purification, told Sorfon every soul deserves redemption and asked him to get Locus out of the city and away from La Toma — pointing him toward an old ally and toward the links Ereldra keeps hidden. The Geas blocks Locus's memory and compels him, and lifts only when Strahd, his likely ancestor, is dead. He travels with the party now, and must be kept out of the Shadowfell. On the mountain above Vasselheim he tasted a drop of human blood: veins rose across his face, his eyes darkened, and he began tracking the wounded by their blood, barely in control.

title: The Axe and the Corrupted Dragon
summary: Bahamut explained why the ancient black dragon Haftifaflmorhen keeps appearing: tricked by Torog (?) and forced to devour his best friend, he is a maddened victim who hunts the Barûk-Kazad. The Platinum Dragon refused to take the axe off their hands: it stays under guard in Kraghammer, but Ereldra can call it to her as her pact weapon, so the party still answers for it and tells no one where it lies — the more so because her patron Ashardalon would be served by it. Peace comes only when the axe returns to its maker. Pelor has since named the corrupter: Torog, the Crawling King, the last Betrayer God he cast down, working from his prison in the Far Realm — and counselled that saving or killing Haftifaflmorhen ends the same, since his mind is gone. The party's decision: keep the axe, give it to no dragon, and trap the dragon and grant him rest once they are strong enough. A letter to the Council of Kraghammer now tells them the party will call the axe to use as bait, its return promised; leave should come within a day.

title: The Patron in the Hoard
summary: Mid-crossing the ancient red dragon Ashardalon reached Ereldra from atop a vast hoard, claiming her as patron and demanding to know why the party strayed from Whitestone. She professes loyalty while serving the patron's true objective, bound up with the de Rolo line. In council she admitted outright that Ashardalon's plan is genocide, and the party resolved that he gets no axe from them — while in an old nightmare of Mortis's, Torog offered to take Ashardalon's place at her shoulder. Then her soul was dragged on an astral journey to the Nine Hells, where Ashardalon besieges Dis with infernal machines that burn refined residuum. He wants the white stone beneath Whitestone, refined, and gave her a black parchment: pour a lamb's blood on it and any residuum thrown upon it goes straight to him. Of his fourteen warlocks she works best. Percy recognised his own black-powder design in the machines, and the party means to have her deliver residuum blended to wreck them.

title: The Vampire of Ravenloft
summary: The Raven Queen told Mortis that Ravenloft and Barovia were torn out of her realm and are held illegitimately by the vampire Strahd von Zarovich — who bred Locus to be his hound and still means to have him. Strahd cannot be reached yet: when the party is ready to cross the Shadowfell they are to seek Vax'ildan, her champion, who will guide them. Until then Locus stays out of the Shadowfell, where Strahd would sense him, and his Geas cannot be broken while Strahd lives. Percy had never heard of Strahd or Barovia, and no map the party carries shows it; Mortis remembers Ravenloft as one of the few floating cities of the Age of Arcanum, spared the Calamity when the von Zarovich family, who had stolen it, drew it into the Shadowfell.

title: The Fourteen
summary: Ashardalon keeps fourteen warlocks and plays them against one another: the one who brings him residuum wins his favour, and the rest are cast aside. Ereldra is the one who 'works best' — so, Fungrim (?) warns, the patron has told the others she must die. Fungrim, a half-mad dwarf who fought Haftifaflmorhen at Kraghammer and gave her a burr pendant that calls him, refused. Elías did not: from a cave on the mountain some 3 km away he fired on the party at the Temple of Sarenrae, his invisible imp familiar spotting for him and lying that its master was Fungrim. The party went after him on the mountain above Vasselheim: Fungrim staged a fight, Mortis took Ereldra's shape and Ayante ran up alone — to be caught by Elías, chained by an imp and shot up when he fought back. The hunt came to a head in a clearing, where the imp's bomb and Elías's shots struck again and Sorfon's spirit Aldis faded shielding him; Elías still stands, pistol in hand.

title: The Debt to Allura
summary: After Allura Vysoren bound the ghostly Mortis and named the party his wardens, they owe her a mission to repair the damage done to Greyskull Keep. The nature of that mission has not yet been revealed.

title: The Lost Temple of Sarenrae
summary: Sorfon came to Tal'Dorei hunting the ancient temple where his mother trained. Sarenrae, angered by his lifelong devotion to Pelor alone, gave only a riddle: 'The temple is just a temple; follow YOUR light.' Pike Trickfoot, the one who knew the way, was finally found tending the gardens of the Temple of Sarenrae in Vasselheim, and marked the ancient temple on the party's map of Issylra: about 27 km north of the city, in the mountains. Percy has agreed to stop there on the way to Whitestone.

title: Ayante's Aristeia
summary: Sent abroad from Ilión, Ayante seeks the great deed his city will remember, and records every step of the journey in a codex to be delivered home. He believes his aristeia lies somewhere along Sorfon's road.

title: The Forge of Tyr
summary: The commissions left with Tyr came back finished. Ayante was given the Helm of the Wrathbringer (?) for nothing — it makes foes fear him, so long as his head stays on his shoulders — and Sorfon's old chainmail was reforged into the Plate of Knights' Fellowship (AC 18), stamped with the Dwendalian owl-eyes. A one-eyed soldier's spirit, Aldis (?), is caught in the metal and can be summoned as an ally each fight; he served the Empire and knew a Cousland, and the plate once belonged to Gerard Cousland (?), likely Sorfon's kin.

title: The Audience in the Shadowfell
summary: Mortis died by his own hand to cross into the Shadowfell and stand before the Raven Queen. She named Strahd the thief of Ravenloft and Barovia, named Locus the hound bred for him, and named Vax'ildan the guide who can bring the party across when they are ready — then sent Mortis back with the charge to finish the main mission first.

title: The Journey to the Hells
summary: Ereldra's eye caught fire and her soul, trailing a silver thread, was dragged to the Nine Hells while her body bled in Vasselheim. She watched Ashardalon's infernal machines besiege Dis, blinked across the battlefield to his side and heard his demand: the refined white stone of Whitestone, sent through a black parchment. He crushed the imp spying on her and sent her back.

title: The Meeting with Bahamut
summary: The white-robed man from the crossroads, the Archon who governs Vasselheim this cycle, revealed himself at the palace gate as Bahamut, the Platinum Dragon. He named Haftifaflmorhen a victim of Torog (?), recalled the Calamity and his lost companion Cromulus (?), declined to accept the Barûk-Kazad, and told Sorfon and Ereldra to keep its location secret for now.

title: Delivering the Barûk-Kazad
summary: The party returned the legendary dwarven axe to Kraghammer and escorted Cassandra's body from the ruined palace, claiming both bounties for 4,800 gp. Sorfon was named Emissary of Kraghammer. The axe stayed behind under guard — though it is Ereldra's pact weapon, and she can summon it to her hand wherever she is.

title: Caval's Grave and the Witch's Book
summary: Ereldra found Caval's grave in the crypt and Mortis told her of his betrayer. Above ground the party settled Baba Yaga's book — bound in skin, clasped with teeth — stowing it in the bag of holding rather than burning it back to the witch.

title: The Pact Beneath the Sun
summary: At Gilmore's shop in Emon, Ayante overheard Sorfon asking after an ancient temple. Mockery gave way to respect once he learned Sorfon served Pelor, and the two devotees sealed a pact bare-armed beneath the noon sun.
